title: Everyday Algorithm Auditing: Understanding the Power of Everyday Users in Surfacing Harmful Algorithmic Behaviors
reasoning: The paper investigates the sociotechnical process of how everyday users detect and report algorithmic bias (such as racial and gender bias) through case studies. While it discusses 'harmful behaviors' and mentions religious sites being misclassified as an example of a bias blindspot, it does not evaluate or benchmark religion, morals, or ethics as a primary component of its research.
